questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Keep proper distance from other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep proper distance from other riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. Check your mirrors often to see riders behind you. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep enough space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: Each traffic lane gives a motorcycle rider how many paths to travel?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection all the time to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if they wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection all the time to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage over time, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs and other hearing protection can help prevent this damage while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Should be avoided because it causes heat problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to other safety benefits.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.
Tell them to take quiet roads instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take quiet roads instead.
questions.explanation: To prevent someone from riding while drunk, arrange other transportation, keep them busy to slow their drinking, find excuses to delay them until they are sober, and ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops instead of or along with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means the rider plans to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A child passenger should:

options.text: Sit in front of the operator.
Not need to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. A child in front may lose balance and get in the way of the operator's controls.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: To swerve correctly:

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Push the handgrip away from the turn direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side you want to turn. After you clear the hazard, push the opposite handgrip to go back to your original direction.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you wish to turn.
Avoid dragging your feet on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road, as they could catch on something and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, where should you place heavier items?
questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load, over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space for better visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, where should a motorcycle operator position themselves?

options.text: Always in the same part of the lane.
In different positions based on road and traffic conditions.
Always in the center of the lane.
Always on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In different positions based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks collision. Riding on the far side may tempt the driver to re-enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: What is found in the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best part of the lane for a motorcycle.
Oil and grease, but it is usually safe for riding.
Oil and grease, and it is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oil and grease, but it is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars collect in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this area is usually safe to ride. Avoid large buildups of oil and grease at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which adjustment is NOT needed?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, adjust tire pressure, suspension, headlight, and mirrors for the extra weight. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: The group takes up less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
Riders reach their destination faster than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group uses less road space, is easier to see, and stays together at traffic lights. However, the speed of arrival is the same whether the group is close or spread out.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: When it is raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, the road is slippery because oil has not washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often your best choice.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: Turn only your head to look through the turn. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When following a car, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. The driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the best formation for a group of riders going into a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when taking curves or turning. This formation is safer for curves, turns, and highway entrances and exits.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue while riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress properly to protect yourself from wind and rain, which cause fatigue. Limit rides to about six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should you NOT use?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider.
Minimize breaks so riders reach their destination quickly.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Keep the group in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Minimize breaks so riders reach their destination quickly.
questions.explanation: Plan trip length based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind leaders so experienced riders can watch them. Use a staggered formation for safety.
